title: R4/B56 resource denominator for Runtime blocking I/O
author_role: local candidate author; not G acceptance or integration publication
decision_question: Does B56's specified shared capacity include every Runtime blocking-I/O operation, or does it bound scientific method/fold work while Runtime I/O has its own explicitly bounded process capacity?

authority_and_scope.authority_source: No external issuer, production workload, law, or institutional authority is claimed. G retains independent code acceptance and formal finding adjudication.
authority_and_scope.time_scope: source-bound local diagnostic on 2026-10-15; no live production currentness claim
authority_and_scope.workload_scope: The R4 fixture is a portable deterministic two-study synthetic workload. It is not a qualifying production workload.
authority_and_scope.surface_scope: Runtime internal blocking dependency guards and their process executor; no public API, authorization, or policy-status semantics are changed by this packet.

relevant_spans.text: The example is 15 fold workers per fit and 60 theoretical workers from four simultaneous fits; the card explicitly calls this capacity arithmetic, not observed CPU load or measured slowdown.
The recommended first route is existing max_parallel_folds passed from the actual study resource, and the card says a new cluster scheduler is unnecessary.
If shared admission is needed, avoid a cycle where outer work occupies every resource while waiting for inner tasks on the same resource.
For a specified shared resource, bound the sum of admitted work, preserve folds/repeats/results/provenance, and measure elapsed time, peak memory, active workers, and waiting.
The card describes composition/configuration, not a proven defect in one run or a universal fixed capacity.

original_criterion.denominator_reading: The text ties the resource to fit/fold admission, but never defines its denominator as every Runtime blocking-I/O thread. Reading B56 as the scientific method/fold budget is the closest fit to its max_parallel_folds recommendation; extending it to all CAS/control-store work is a new resource-boundary decision for G, not a fact established by the card.

profile.timeout_semantics: BlockingDependencyGuard submits to the configured executor and then calls future.result(timeout=1.5); this is an end-to-end submit/queue/service deadline.

observed_r4_failure.workload: Two isolated Runtime/CAS roots; actual ControlWorker, RunLifecycle, run_experiment, causal node, MethodBackend, dispatcher, TMLE fold path, and FileSystemCAS writes. 240-row paired synthetic HTE inputs, seeds 811/812; 3 folds x 2 repeats per study. The causal safety admission gate was bypassed only to isolate B56 admission; no safety/promotion claim is made.
observed_r4_failure.interpretation: Both callers timed out on queue plus service; the actual writes completed later. The observed caller failure is neither nested self-wait nor a CAS operation failure. The R4 child failed before terminal control-job/result readback, so all 12 folds, complete results, provenance, and fresh GETs remain not_established.
observed_r4_failure.exact_payload_profile_limitation: cas-1274/cas-1275 are observer operation IDs, not ArtifactRefs. The diagnostic intentionally retained operation name/timing/thread/executor state but not put_json arguments, canonical payload size/hash, or artifact reference. The pytest temp root recorded in stdout no longer exists. Therefore an exact cProfile of those two failed payloads cannot be reconstructed from retained evidence; profiling a surrogate as if it were exact would be false.

last_ordinary_engineering_investigation.question: Could a generic CAS redundant-work optimization remove enough service time to make both queued calls fit the unchanged 1.5-second deadline under the existing shared capacity?

actual_source_observation.put_json_calls_to_canonicalization: policy-engine/src/polisyos/core/artifacts/store.py:2951-2952 calls to_canonical_bytes(obj, spec) and then calls the same _validate_core_json_payload_conformance(data, spec) again. to_canonical_bytes itself performs this conformance validation at policy-engine/src/polisyos/core/canon/canon_json.py:67-75.
actual_source_observation.property_to_preserve: Canonical/profile refusal and exact bytes remain authoritative. The in-memory probe removed only the repeated store-module validation call; to_canonical_bytes' own conformance validation remained active, and the actual FileSystemCAS transaction, owner checks, manifest publication, and verify remained active.

bounded_actual_profile.input: Exact paired 240-row HTE observational-data generator and ArtifactWriteOptions/CAS profile from test_r4_shared_study_admission.py:417-440, seeds 811/812; one fresh filesystem CAS root per study; no injected delay and no concurrent workload.
bounded_actual_profile.guard_profile: Actual BlockingDependencyGuard over the shared executor, capacity 1 revision r4-native-method-cap-1-v1; unchanged 1.5-second deadline.
bounded_actual_profile.interpretation: The in-memory one-repeat probe reduced this 42 KB input write by about 24.4-24.5% under cProfile, with identical ArtifactIDs and successful verification. It is a real no-delay FileSystemCAS/guard profile, but not the timed output payloads and not a concurrent R4 proof. On this input it saves about 9 ms, far below the roughly 198-216 ms caller overrun; unknown timed payload size/content prevents extrapolating that ratio to cas-1274/1275. It therefore does not establish that redundant-work removal alone can fix R4.

last_ordinary_engineering_investigation.engineering_conclusion: Keep the duplicate-validation removal as a small source-level candidate for separate review because it preserves the validation performed by to_canonical_bytes. Do not use this 42 KB profile to explain or close the 0.86-second service hotspot. To decide whether it suffices, instrument cProfile around the exact two actual put_json callables in a new source-frozen R4 diagnostic and retain only safe aggregate timing/profile metadata; if the optimization cannot bring both complete callers below 1.5 seconds while retaining all artifacts, it is not the capacity solution. No source change was made in this investigation.

decision_options.meaning: The B56 shared-cap denominator includes scientific work plus every Runtime blocking CAS/control-store operation on the process shared executor.
benefits: One physical worker-cap invariant; no additional runtime thread vector.
Matches current executor wiring and makes the total worker count easy to measure.
costs_and_open_questions: A cap-1 caller can be behind another method or blocking operation; the observed two calls exceed 1.5 seconds even though their CAS operations succeed later.
The only identified no-semantics micro-optimization is not shown to recover the required 198-216 ms on the actual payloads.
Must show cap-1 work waits without lost/failed jobs and preserve every fold/result; otherwise document a specific bounded residual rather than claiming B56 closure.

decision_options.meaning: B56 capacity governs method/fold compute admission; Runtime blocking I/O receives a distinct, explicitly bounded, process-scoped capacity profile with one owner shared by all relevant Runtime guards.
decision_options.current_deadline: Preserve the 1.5-second end-to-end CAS and control-store deadlines; do not split queue/service budgets.
benefits: Matches B56's concrete max_parallel_folds/current-study-resource route while making I/O concurrency explicit instead of silently unbounded.
Lets I/O progress while compute workers are occupied, without claiming a production-capacity value.
costs_and_open_questions: Total process workers may exceed the B56 compute cap; that is a new explicit resource-vector semantics requiring G's choice.

For this particular pair of independent ~0.86-second writes, a one-worker I/O pool would still serialize the second call past 1.5 seconds; two simultaneous I/O slots are a minimum experiment for this paired case, not a default or production capacity recommendation.

The process owner must share one profile across 2+ Runtime instances and all CAS/control-store guards, bound backlog, preserve tenant/context propagation, and define cancellation, late completion, shutdown, and same-pool reentrancy behavior.

The existing CAS and control-store *_EXECUTOR_MAX_WORKERS settings are passed alongside get_shared_executor(); they do not create dedicated pools in the current builders. Turning them into per-guard pools would multiply capacity and is not acceptable.
decision_options.status: locally recommended interpretation; requires G decision before implementation

decision_options.meaning: Increase the total deadline or split queue-wait and service budgets.
decision_options.current_deadline: Would change the current 1.5-second max-call behavior documented for Runtime CAS.
benefits: Could let queued operations finish without adding worker capacity.
costs_and_open_questions: Changes timeout/504 behavior and may retain requests past the existing bound.
Does not fix the measured capacity queue and can hide a nested-wait cycle; needs a separately owned SLO/authority decision.
decision_options.status: not recommended absent an explicit G decision; not implemented

minimum_g_choice: Decide whether B56's shared resource denominator means compute/fold admission only or all Runtime blocking I/O calls. If compute/fold only, authorize a named bounded process Runtime-I/O profile while preserving 1.5-second total guard deadlines. If aggregate, retain a single pool and require an exact-payload profile plus a cap-1 falsifier before claiming the CAS optimization solves the issue.

candidate_recommendation.choice: Interpret B56 as method/fold compute capacity and prototype a separate bounded process-scoped Runtime I/O profile, while retaining the current 1.5-second end-to-end deadlines.
candidate_recommendation.basis: The original B56 recommendation routes max_parallel_folds from the actual study resource; it does not explicitly include CAS/control-store I/O. Current source implementation reuses one executor for those unrelated blocking calls, which is a wiring choice rather than clear B56 criterion text.
candidate_recommendation.status: proposal_only; not accepted; do not report formal B56 closure

migration_if_G_selects_vector.typed_contract: Add a candidate-only, process-scoped RuntimeBlockingIoProfile with positive bounded capacity and required revision; preserve SharedExecutorProfile as the method/fold compute profile. Conflicting process configuration fails closed.
migration_if_G_selects_vector.owner_lifecycle: One process owner is shared by all CAS/control-store guards across Runtime instances; per-Runtime close must not shut down a sibling's pool. Explicit shutdown occurs only at the process owner boundary.
migration_if_G_selects_vector.boundedness: Bound both running I/O calls and pending submissions; over-cap wait/rejection is typed, visible, and cannot silently drop CAS operations. Preserve tenant/contextvars. Same-pool reentry and cancelled-but-running writes receive explicit behavior.
migration_if_G_selects_vector.existing_configuration: Resolve the presently ineffective CAS/control-store *_EXECUTOR_MAX_WORKERS settings into one typed profile or deprecate them explicitly; never instantiate one pool per guard. No environment-only or per-Runtime capacity multiplication.
migration_if_G_selects_vector.deadline_and_status: Keep existing 1.5-second total call timeout. A timed-out write remains a possibly-late durable operation; caller status and subsequent durable readback must remain explicit.
migration_if_G_selects_vector.no_new_claim: No production capacity/currentness, causal workload adequacy, or external authority claim follows from the synthetic profile.

required_falsifiers_before_any_r4_propos: Source-freeze the exact selected implementation, all tests/facades/config/docs companions, and all affected runtime/profile hashes before the expensive wave.

Capture cProfile of the exact two slow put_json operations with privacy-safe size/type/phase counters and no payloads; compare an in-memory or source-level duplicate-validation removal while keeping to_canonical_bytes and manifest/content checks intact. Decide whether it alone puts both calls under 1.5 seconds; otherwise reject it as sufficient.

Run one composed source-bound R4 cap-1, cap-2, and bridge-removal wave after independent review: actual physical compute/I/O active peaks and full queue roster; no nested self-wait; bounded pending queue; cancellation/late completion behavior; all 12 folds with seeds/provenance; both control jobs terminal; results/evidence read through fresh CAS instances; exact output equality and removal behavior.

Test 2+ Runtime instances sharing one bounded process I/O owner, multiple CAS proxies, sibling usability after one Runtime closes, profile conflict rejection, timeout with service-only delay, and control-store contention or a named bounded residual.
Keep the profile candidate-only; do not claim this local synthetic witness establishes a production workload or any institutional capacity authorization.

pattern_pass.anti_pattern_found: The generic Runtime shared executor currently combines compute admission and blocking storage guards; the guard's 1.5s timer measures queue plus service. A CAS worker env field suggests independent capacity although the builder passes the canonical shared executor. This is a boundary/measurement mismatch, not evidence of an external authority fact.
pattern_pass.target_pattern: Name each capacity denominator, use one typed process owner per bounded resource, measure actual admitted/queued work, preserve status for late writes, and verify the real consumer path with removal and complete output readback.
pattern_pass.capability_state: R4 is verification_missing for complete cap-1/cap-2/removal readback; a capacity-vector contract is decision_pending, not a new accepted capability.

current_process_capacity_owner.finding: A process-scoped SharedExecutorProfile and shared executor already exist and are reused by CAS and control-store guards. There is no separate bounded Runtime I/O pool/profile to reuse. Its capacity is generic executor capacity, currently shared with MethodBackend compute.

existing_cas_reuse.finding: FileSystemCAS already hashes content and is idempotent/content-addressed. Existing blob reuse still validates the stored bytes and current input ownership/manifest transaction; it does not provide cross-root write coalescing. The two R4 Runtime instances have isolated CAS roots, so a shared-cache shortcut would change ownership/durability boundaries and is not a safe reuse path.

cache_route.finding: The existing caching artifact adapter wraps object-backed S3/GCS stores; R4 uses independent local FileSystemCAS roots. This cache is not on the measured path and cannot be presumed to remove the calls.

smallest_candidate_without_new_capacity_.change: Remove only the second Core conformance round-trip in FileSystemCAS.put_json after to_canonical_bytes has already validated those exact bytes against the same CanonSpec; keep canonicalization refusal, content hash, input-owner checks, manifest generation/validation, durable transaction, and verify unchanged.
smallest_candidate_without_new_capacity_.status: unimplemented source candidate; only the ignored in-memory microprobe was run
smallest_candidate_without_new_capacity_.falsifier: The exact operation cProfile shows the duplicated pass contributes less than the measured caller overrun, or the source-level removal fails canonical malformed-input/refusal, selected-profile, ownership, and persisted-byte drift controls. In either case it cannot be claimed as the R4 capacity fix.
